info.name: 03 - QualityLab Banking
info.description:
Accounts, balances, deposits, withdrawals, transfers and transaction history for the test customer.

Amounts are small and random. The 10,000.00 limit test deposits and then withdraws the same amount.
Deposits, withdrawals and transfers cannot be undone, so they stay in the customer's history.
More amount and transfer cases are in the data-driven collections "Amount boundaries" and "Invalid transfers".

exec: * DYNAMIC TOKEN HANDLING (runs before every request in this collection)
* A request that needs a session sends the header
* where <module> is ecommerce, banking, travel or admin. Each sign-in opens one module, so
* there is one token per module.
* This script looks at that header. If the token for that module is missing, or expires within
* a minute, it signs in first with pm.sendRequest, using the credentials from the environment
* (testUsername/testPassword, or adminUsername/adminPassword for admin), and saves the token
* and its expiry time as collection variables. Postman waits for the sign-in to finish before
* Requests in this collection have Settings > "Disable cookie jar" on, so they authenticate with
* the Bearer token only. pm.sendRequest still uses the cookie jar, so after each sign-in this
* script clears the session cookie it received.
`Set ${admin ? 'adminUsername and adminPassword' : 'testUsername and testPassword'} in the selected environment (Current value).`,
body: { mode: 'raw', raw: JSON.stringify({ email, password, module }) },
throw new Error(`Automatic sign-in to ${module} failed: ${error ? error.message : `${response.code} ${response.text()}`}`);
// The sign-in also stored the app's session cookie. If it stayed, the next automatic
// sign-in would send it, and the app would end that session (and so this token).
'Could not clear the session cookie. In Postman, open Cookies > Domains Allowlist and add the API domain ' +
'(for example quality-lab-jb.vercel.app), or tokens of other modules may stop working.',
